mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions "the difference between the number of X and Y have", interpret it as the signed subtraction X − Y, preserving the order of the names, rather than as an absolute value. This yields a linear equation that may be negative if the narrative forces it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever you see a phrase like "difference between the number of ... that X and Y have" in any equation.
mathgap.example: Treating "the difference between the number of onions that Royal and Marian have" as |Royal − Marian| instead of Royal − Marian, which creates ambiguous or wrong solutions.

mathgap.title: Directed "has more than" Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form "A has N more than B" into the equation A − B = N, preserving direction, and do not enforce that the difference must be positive; allow negative values if other constraints require it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct comparison using "has N more than" appears.
mathgap.example: Assuming "Marian has 5 more onions than Royal" forces Royal > Marian and discarding the solution Royal − Marian = ‑5.

mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Process each "A gives N onions to B" statement in the order it appears, immediately subtracting N from A's current count and adding N to B's current count, because later statements refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer ("gives ... to ...") statement is encountered.
mathgap.example: Applying all transfers only after parsing the whole problem, so a later equation uses outdated counts for the giver or receiver.

mathgap.title: Immediate Count Update on Direct Assignment
mathgap.principle: Treat each direct count statement "A has N onions" as setting A's current count at that point, overriding any previous value (including after earlier transfers). Subsequent statements use this updated count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count statement appears in the text.
mathgap.example: Treating "Aileen has 22 onions" as an initial value only and not updating Aileen's count after a preceding transfer involving Aileen.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in Difference Equations
mathgap.principle: For statements like "The number of onions that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of onions that C and D have", construct the equation (A − B) = (C − D) exactly as written, keeping the order of C and D; do not swap them or take an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing relational equations that equate one difference to another.
mathgap.example: Writing the equation as (A − B) = (D − C) or using |C − D| instead of C − D, which changes the solution.

mathgap.description: Interpreting "difference between X and Y" as an absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The word "difference" often suggests magnitude, leading solvers to take the absolute value.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the names and use X − Y as a signed expression, not |X − Y|.

mathgap.description: Applying all transfers after processing other statements, ignoring their sequential effect.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Transfers are seen as independent net changes, so solvers delay their application.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Update the giver and receiver immediately when a transfer statement is read, before any later statements that involve them.

mathgap.description: Assuming "A has N more than B" implies A > B and discarding solutions where the computed difference is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Natural‑language intuition that "more than" means a larger quantity.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat the relation as A − B = N without imposing a positivity constraint; allow negative differences if other equations force them.

mathgap.description: Reversing the order of variables on the right‑hand side of a difference equation.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Misreading "difference between X and Y" as an unordered pair.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the exact order of the names when forming the subtraction (X − Y).

mathgap.description: Treating a direct count statement as an immutable initial value and not updating it after earlier transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Assuming all "has N" statements refer to the starting configuration.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, set the person's current count to that number at that point, overriding any previous value.
